title: Leeward 02: The Sea Fight, Naval Battle Sound Effects
shortText: 124 naval battle sound effects: incoming shot, hull hits, splinters, fire aboard, boarding, sinking. WAV + OGG.
html:
The same ship as Leeward, taken into a fight: incoming shot, hull hits, fire aboard, boarding and the sinking

124 naval battle sound effects: shot whistling in at four ranges, near misses by calibre, round, chain and grape shot striking the ship heard on deck, below decks and from another ship, splinters, a topmast going over, fire aboard you turn up a tier at a time, the pumps, a list, the sinking, boarding with steel and flintlocks, the battle heard from three distances and 19 seamless loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 26 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. One round shot heard on deck, below decks and from another ship, the shot whistling in at all four ranges, the three fire tiers to stack yourself, a whole boarding from grapnel to hulls meeting, and the smallest and biggest near miss.

What is in it

  • Incoming fire (13)
  • Near misses (11)
  • Strikes (25)
  • Rig damage (10)
  • Fire aboard (13)
  • Damage control (9)
  • List and strain (5)
  • Sinking (6)
  • Boarding (26)
  • Battle beds (6)

The half of a sea battle Leeward did not have

Leeward is one ship at sea and in harbour, and it fires its guns. This pack is what lands: the receiving side a fight repeats dozens of times, shipped as 23 take sets so a battle does not machine gun one file (hull hits, shot through the hull below, splinter showers, near miss splashes, axe chops, parries, pistol shots). It is built from the same hand authored material tables as Leeward, oak, pine, hemp, iron, canvas and water made of ringing bubbles, so the two packs are one vessel. None of Leeward's files is repeated: 16 overlapping roles were measured against Leeward from both packs' audio and every one is a different sound.

Every strike heard from three places

Round shot smashes the side, chain shot tears the rigging, grapeshot sweeps the deck, and each ships as heard on deck, below decks (where a round shot comes through the side among you) and from another ship across the water. 9 perspective pairs and 9 projectile pairs measured apart on the shipped files, 0 too close.

Range, calibre, flow and distance

A round shot whistling in from overhead to far off; near misses from a swivel gun to a 32 pounder; a shot hole leaking from a trickle to a flood; the battle close by, at a mile and on the horizon. Each rung is darker than the one before it, so you pick the file by how far, how big and how bad (10 steps measured, 0 failing).

Fire aboard, and four lifecycles

Fire is three loops of one length: a smoulder, flames, the deck alight. Fade a tier in as it spreads; every one of the 3 stacks is re-summed from the shipped files and wraps cleanly. Chain pump, Fire aboard, Boarding, The sinking each ship as a start, a seamless loop while it runs, a stop and, where there is one, the way it fails (the pump chokes, the fire flares up, the grapnel slips). 15 states, every loop flag read out of the file.

Already own our other packs?

Where this pack fills a role Sixgun, Squall, Steel and Bone, Wade, Pithead or Portcullis already fills (a fire, an explosion, a parry, a big splash), the two were measured against each other from both packs' files: 17 more shared roles, every one a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 19 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV

loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 2.1 dB, explosions included.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1147 checks, 0 failed.
  • No voices and nothing musical, so it sits under any score and any crew.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings of real ships or guns, and there are no voices: no shouted orders, no cries. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Leeward: Ships, Sea and Harbour, the same ship at sea and in harbour: rigging, hull, canvas, the gun deck, the bell and seven places.
  • Broadside, a naval battle plugin for RPG Maker MZ from the same studio, drawing holed planking, a fallen topmast, fire on deck and boarding.
  • Saltline: A Voyage and Harbour Score, music for the voyage, from the same studio.
  • Squall: Weather Systems, rain, wind and storms as layers you drive with one value.
